parts.latex: Which inequality gives the domain of $y=\sqrt{2x-3}$?

solutions.latex:
The expression under the square root cannot be negative:
$$\begin{aligned} 2x-3&\ge 0\\ x&\ge \dfrac{3}{2}\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: Which of the following represents the domain of the function $f(x)=\ln(1-x)$?

solutions.latex:
The logarithm is only defined for positive arguments:
$$\begin{aligned} 1 - x &> 0 \\ x &< 1 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{domain} = (-\infty, 1)$$

parts.latex:
Let $h(x)=f(g(x))$ where the function $f(x)$ is an odd function and the function $g(x)$ is an even function.

The tangent to $y=h(x)$ at $x=k$, where $k>0$, has the equation $y=mx+c$.

What is the equation of the tangent to $y=h(x)$ at $x=-k$?

solutions.latex:
$g$ is even, so $h(-x) = f\big(g(-x)\big) = f\big(g(x)\big) = h(x)$: $h$ is an even function.

The graph of an even function is symmetric about the $y$-axis, so
$$h(-k) = h(k) = mk + c \qquad\text{and}\qquad h'(-k) = -h'(k) = -m$$
Tangent at $x = -k$:
$$\begin{aligned} y - (mk + c) &= -m(x + k) \\ y &= -mx - mk + mk + c \\ y &= -mx + c \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: Which of the following is the range of the function $f(x)=x^2-1$?

solutions.latex:
$x^2 \ge 0$ for all real $x$, so
$$f(x) = x^2 - 1 \ge -1$$
and $f(x)$ takes every value from $-1$ upwards (the minimum $-1$ is at $x = 0$).
$$\therefore\ \text{range} = [-1, \infty)$$

solutions.latex:

parts.latex:
Let $f(x)$ be any function with domain all real numbers.

Which of the following is an even function, regardless of the choice of $f(x)$?

solutions.latex:
Let $h(x) = f(x)f(-x)$. Replacing $x$ by $-x$:
$$h(-x) = f(-x)f(x) = h(x)$$
so $h$ is even for every function $f$.

The others depend on $f$: for example, with $f(x) = x$, the functions $2f(x) = 2x$ and $f\big(f(x)\big) = x$ are odd, and with $f(x) = x + 1$, $\big(f(-x)\big)^2 = (1-x)^2$ is not even.

parts.latex: If $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ and $g(x)=4-x^2$, what is the domain of the function $f(g(x))$ ?

parts.latex: If $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ and $g(x)=\ln(x-1)$, what is the domain of the composite function $f(g(x))$?

solutions.latex:
$$f(g(x))=\sqrt{\ln(x-1)}$$
Conditions:

$\ln(x-1)$ is defined: $x-1>0$, so $x>1$.

The square root needs a non-negative input: $\ln(x-1)\ge 0$.
$$\begin{aligned} \ln(x-1)&\ge 0\\ x-1&\ge 1 \quad(\text{since } \ln 1=0 \text{ and } \ln \text{ is increasing})\\ x&\ge 2 \end{aligned}$$
$x\ge2$ also satisfies $x>1$.

$\therefore$ Domain: $[2,\infty)$

parts.latex: What is the domain of the function $y=\sqrt{6-x^2}$?

solutions.latex:
The square root is defined only when $6-x^2\ge 0$:
$$x^2 \le 6$$
$$-\sqrt{6} \le x \le \sqrt{6}$$
The endpoints are included since $\sqrt{0}=0$ is defined.

So the domain is $\left[-\sqrt{6},\sqrt{6}\,\right]$.

parts.latex:
It is given that $h(x)=\sin^2 x-\sin x$ is a composite function of $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ where $f(x)=x^2-x$ and $g(x)=\sin x$ for all real values of $x$.

For what values of $k$ does the equation $\sin^2 x-\sin x=k$ have real solutions?

solutions.latex:
Let $u=\sin x$, so $-1\le u\le 1$ and $k=u^2-u$.

The parabola $k=u^2-u$ has its vertex at $u=\dfrac{1}{2}$, which lies in $[-1,1]$:
$$k=\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2-\dfrac{1}{2}=-\dfrac{1}{4}$$
At the end points, $u=-1$ gives $k=2$ and $u=1$ gives $k=0$.
$$\therefore\ -\dfrac{1}{4}\le k\le 2$$

parts.latex:
Let $f(x)$ be a continuous and differentiable function for all real values of $x$.

The following facts are known.

\begin{itemize}
\item $f'(-x)=f'(x)$
\item $f'(x)\neq0$
\item $f(0)=f''(0)=0$
\end{itemize}

parts.latex: If $f(x)=|x|$ and $g(x)$ is the new function after $f(x)$ is dilated horizontally by factor $\dfrac{1}{5}$ and shifted down 2 units, what is the range of $g(x)$?

A horizontal dilation by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{5}$ replaces $x$ by $\dfrac{x}{\frac{1}{5}}=5x$; a shift down 2 replaces $y$ by $y+2$.
